terminal_artifact: Approved CalFresh certification with benefits posted to an EBT account (card and PIN mailed separately, or picked up at the district office), plus an approval Notice of Action stating the allotment, household size, certification period and IRT limit
denial_rate_notes: From G3: LA County's average CalFresh approval rate was 48 percent before the flexible-interview work (DPSS set a goal of 60 percent), implying a 52 percent denial rate; one in three applications were denied for a missed interview while only 6 percent were denied for ineligibility. The randomized trial moved approval from 58 percent (control) to 61 percent (treatment) among GetCalFresh-assisted applicants, so the 48 percent baseline and the 58/61 percent trial figures are different populations and should not be mixed.

timing_gold.source: audit (randomized controlled trial of LA County applicants assisted by GetCalFresh, reported by Code for America with researchers at NYU and the Federal Reserve Bank of New York)
timing_gold.quote: the average time to determination for applicants in the treatment group (including those who used the flexible interview line and those who did not) was 15 days, compared to just under 19 days for applicants in the control group

timing_gold_secondary.what: Statutory and regulatory ceiling for normal processing
timing_gold_secondary.value: 30 calendar days from the application date, with day zero being the day the application is received
timing_gold_secondary.quote: The normal processing timeframe for an application is 30 calendar days. A determination of eligibility on a submitted application must be made as soon as administratively possible, but no later than 30 calendar days following the application date.

timing_gold_secondary.what: Expedited service: California's own deadline is stricter than the federal floor
timing_gold_secondary.value: 3 calendar days (state, AB 2384 as amended by AB 1359) versus 7 calendar days (federal floor, 7 C.F.R. § 273.2(i)(3)(i)); a weekend counts as one calendar day and a day-three holiday or weekend pulls the deadline to the preceding business day
timing_gold_secondary.quote: Process applications for households entitled to ES within three calendar days [the current federal mandate is seven days under 7 Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) Section 273.2 (i)(3)(i)].

timing_gold_secondary.what: Effect of the flexible interview line on the applicants who used it
timing_gold_secondary.value: a determination roughly seven days sooner than control, and 6 percent more likely to be enrolled (an 11 percent increase in the approval rate)
timing_gold_secondary.quote: Applicants who received information about flexible interviews and who called the flexible interview line received a benefit determination roughly seven days sooner than those in the control group

timing_gold_secondary.value: 10 calendar days from the written CW 2200 request, extended to the next business day if day ten is a weekend or holiday
timing_gold_secondary.quote: HHs must be allowed ten calendar days to provide the requested verification(s).

known_gaps: No per-stage timing exists for LA County. G3's 15-day and 19-day figures are end-to-end time-to-determination for one population (GetCalFresh-assisted applicants, in a 2020-2021 pilot), not stage medians. The gold therefore gives statutory deadlines for most activities and a measured median only for F22. CDSS's CalFresh Data Dashboard publishes monthly county timeliness but only behind a Tableau session or Excel download, which was not pulled.

The queue between filing and first worker contact (F07) has no published duration. G3 establishes that the delay exists and is caused by intermediary clerical steps, but neither G1 nor G3 says how long it is, which is precisely the interval a claimant experiences as silence.

G1 does not name the case-management system. Only Santa Clara County's public handbook names CalSAWS; whether LA runs the identical statewide platform is not settled by any document held here, so the system actor (data_interfaces) is modelled by its interfaces rather than by the system of record.

Whether the flexible "end-to-end" interview line (F10) still operates, and whether it was extended beyond GetCalFresh-assisted applicants, is unresolved. G3 reports full rollout to GetCalFresh applicants in May 2021 and no later designed-tier document confirms the current state; G1's 2025 revision only adds 'flexible appointment language' to the GEN 102, which may or may not be the same intervention.

Supervisory gates are not documented. G2 establishes the eligibility supervisor's role in the agency conference (F06), but nothing in G1 or G2 describes supervisor authorization thresholds, second review of denials, or the reopening of auto-closed cases, which county eligibility workers describe in user reports. Those reports are excluded from this gold file.

Several activities are applicant_facing in the sense that the applicant receives an artifact, yet appear in no applicant-facing document in the slug's raw/ corpus: F01 (same-day filing right), F02 (the 19-form intake packet), F06 (the agency conference right), F12 (the mandated at-interview review list and R&R script), F13 (ABAWD screening), F14 (the CF 386 NOMI), F16 (the written IEVS notice), F17 (the CW 2200 by name), F21, F26, F27, F28, F29 and F31 (the CW 10). A solver working from the public footprint can recover the interview, the 10-day proof request, the 30-day clock, the 3-day ES path and the EBT card, and essentially nothing else on this list. That asymmetry is the measurement this task exists for, and it also means the applicant-visible recall denominator is much larger than the declared footprint suggests.

F05 is modelled as one screening activity, but G2 makes clear the screening channel differs by intake route (mail/fax/drop-off/online screened from the application text; telephone and in-person screened during the interview), and the ES-criteria arithmetic (standard utility allowance treatment, liquid-resource counting under Modified Categorical Eligibility) is a decision procedure this schema cannot express.

The gold covers the initial application only. Recertification, the SAR 7 semi-annual report, and the discontinuance-restoration waiver lane are governed by separate chapters (G4 for restoration) and are excluded; the SAR 7 timeline a household actually experiences is in D1 and in Santa Clara's handbook, not here.

G2 is from 2016 and G3 describes 2019-2021 operations, while G1 is current to 01-22-2026. Where they disagree the gold follows G1, but the three documents are not a single snapshot, and G2's ES scripts and forms (DFA 296/296X reporting) have since been superseded.
notes: Gold for the (calfresh, LA County DPSS) task. Designed-tier spine: G1, LA County's own eligibility-staff procedure manual, published live and unauthenticated on the DPSS ePolicy portal and written in the imperative to 'Eligibility staff' — the exact register of back-office gold, with form numbers, clocks and system interfaces a household never sees. G2 (CDSS All County Letter 16-14) supplies the expedited-service spine, the state-versus-federal deadline gap, the agency-conference right, the voicemail scripts and the EBT timeliness rule; it also documents that CDSS had to convene a stakeholder workgroup because county business processes for expedited service were inconsistent, which is the direct evidence that this process varies by county under one statewide mandate. G3 (Code for America) supplies the only measured end-to-end timing and the only account of the clerical-to-worker handoff, from 80+ hours shadowing LA case-opening clerks, eligibility workers, supervisors and office leadership. Declared applicant-facing documents (D1, D2) anchor the five steps an applicant can actually see. Visibility discipline: an activity is labelled staff_only only after confirming that the term appears in no applicant-facing document in corpus/realworld/calfresh/raw/ (checked: 'screen' as ES screening, 'date stamp', 'clerical', 'assign', 'IEVS', 'MEDS', 'electronic source', 'Journal', 'agency conference', 'supervisor', 'CW 2200', 'CF 386', 'GEN 102', 'ABAWD', 'work registration', 'end-to-end', 'flexible' — none appear). The five staff_only activities are F04 (date-stamping and application-date recording), F05 (ES screening), F07 (clerical case assignment), F15 (the mandatory electronic-source check before any verification request) and F30 (Journal-page documentation as a validity condition for a denial). F20 (restarting the ES clock from the date of discovery) is also staff_only: the household cannot observe which clock it is on. Gold-error risk to note: the 19-day median in timing_gold is the control arm of a 2020-2021 randomized trial on GetCalFresh-assisted applicants, which is a selected, digitally-assisted population and probably faster than the LA average; the 48 percent baseline approval rate in denial_rate comes from a different period again.
